correctness.rationale: Pass on /workspace/repairs/5/RESULT.md, not on the frozen proof as printed. Frozen line 54 doubles the first-mode term at opposite centers; the factor must be p(1+c)(1−y). Indeed, (sin a−sin b)²=(1+cos(a+b))(1−cos(a−b)). The erroneous expression already gives the wrong one-arc limit at y=c, whereas the corrected expression gives the printed arc value. The repair also limits the first strict convexity comparison to interior separations, not the antipodal endpoint. Weak-* compactness gives attainment; at any maximizer the nonzero first variation must be maximized as a linear functional, so thresholding its nonconstant degree-two polynomial forces a binary upper-level set of at most two arcs modulo null sets. Complementation reduces to α≤1/2. For fixed positive widths the energy is strictly convex in cos d, so only touching and antipodal centers need be considered. At the latter it is strictly convex in y on [c,1], leaving only the single-arc limit and the equal antipodal pair, including exactly both geometries at a tie. The Toeplitz trace-square calculation counts both directions for each pair and gives the printed weights. The supporting script was inspected, not executed; it checks direct integrations but does not check the erroneous simplified polynomial. Independent exact identities and endpoints were replayed in /workspace/branches/dc685221-6e30-4cd7-9b46-7640afa92cb9/record5_exact_replay.py. The replay is algebraic, not a substitute for the compactness and equality arguments.
